es.summary: El bocio es una ampliación no cancerosa de la glándula tiroides, frecuentemente por deficiencia de yodo o estimulación de TSH. Puede ser estético o causar síntomas de compresión.
key_points: Es más frecuente en áreas con bajo consumo de yodo.
TSH elevada estimula el crecimiento tiroideo.
Puede ser simple (benigno) o asociado a hipertiroidismo/hipotiroidismo.
Complicaciones: dificultad respiratoria, disfagia y posible transformación a nódulo sospechoso.
El tratamiento depende de la causa: suplementación de yodo, levotiroxina o cirugía.

pathophysiology: Deficiencia de yodo reduce la síntesis de T3/T4.
TSH estimula hipertrofia y captación de yodo, aumentando el tamaño glandular.
Acumulación de coloide también contribuye al agrandamiento.
signs_symptoms: Aumento visible del cuello, nódulo anterior.
Sensación de opresión o dificultad para tragar.
Tos seca o ronquera por compresión de la laringe.
En bocio hiperfuncionante: pérdida de peso, temblor, taquicardia.
diagnostics: Palpación y examen físico del cuello.
TSH, T3 y T4 en sangre; TSH alta sugiere bocio simple.
Ecografía tiroidea: evalúa tamaño y presencia de nódulos.
Gammagrafía de tiroides si se sospecha hiperfunción.
Biopsia por aspiración con aguja fina si nódulo sospechoso.
treatment: Suplementación con yodo (ioduro de potasio) en deficiencia.
Levotiroxina si bocio asociado a hipotiroidismo.
Radioyodo o tiroidectomía en bocio grande o sintomático.
complications: Disfagia y sensación de cuerpo extraño.
Transformación a nódulo maligno (cáncer de tiroides).
nursing_care: Evaluar tamaño, consistencia y movilidad del bocio.
Monitorear signos de compromiso respiratorio (frecuencia respiratoria, saturación).
Registrar valores de TSH, T3, T4 y comparar con rangos normales.
Mantener la cabeza del paciente ligeramente elevada para facilitar la respiración.
Preparar al paciente para pruebas diagnósticas (ecografía, biopsia).
patient_teaching: Importancia de una dieta con suficiente yodo (sal yodada, pescados).
Reconocer síntomas de compresión (disnea, dificultad para tragar).
Tomar medicación según prescripción y no suspender sin indicación.

outcomes: Nivel de actividad: tolerará actividades de la vida diaria sin disnea excesiva en 1 semana
Fatiga: reportará disminución de la sensación de cansancio en 5 días

interventions.action: Evaluar frecuencia respiratoria y nivel de esfuerzo al realizar actividades cotidianas.
interventions.rationale: Detectar early signs of intolerance and guide activity modification.

interventions.action: Planificar períodos de descanso cada 20‑30 minutos durante actividades prolongadas.
interventions.rationale: Permite al paciente conservar energía y prevenir agotamiento.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración diafragmática.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la oxigenación y reduce la sensación de falta de aire.

interventions.action: Coordinar con el médico ajuste de antitiroideos o levotiroxina según resultados de laboratorio.
interventions.rationale: Controlar el estado tiroideo reduce los síntomas de intolerancia.

interventions.action: Registrar nivel de cansancio usando escala de 0‑10 antes y después de la actividad.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la evaluación del progreso y la efectividad de intervenciones.

outcomes: No presentará lesiones relacionadas con compromiso respiratorio en 48 horas
Mantendrá integridad cutánea del cuello sin irritación ni úlceras

interventions.action: Observar signos de dificultad respiratoria (cianosis, uso de musculatura accesoria).
interventions.rationale: Identificar rápidamente la necesidad de intervención para prevenir asfixia.

interventions.action: Mantener el área del cuello libre de ropa ajustada y objetos que puedan presionar la glándula.
interventions.rationale: Evita aumento de la compresión y posible lesión cutánea.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de evitar movimientos bruscos del cuello.
interventions.rationale: Reduce el riesgo de traumatismo en una zona ya inflamada.

interventions.action: Colocar al paciente en posición semi‑sentada con respaldo apoyado.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la expansión torácica y disminuye la presión sobre la vía aérea.

interventions.action: Documentar cualquier cambio en el tamaño del bocio y notificar al médico.
interventions.rationale: Permite una intervención oportuna si el bocio progresa.

en.summary: Goiter is a non‑cancerous enlargement of the thyroid gland, often due to iodine deficiency or TSH stimulation. It may be purely cosmetic or cause compression symptoms.
key_points: More common in areas with low iodine intake.
Can be simple (benign) or associated with hyperthyroidism/hypothyroidism.
Complications: respiratory difficulty, dysphagia, and possible transformation to a suspicious nodule.
Treatment depends on cause: iodine supplementation, levothyroxine, or surgery.

pathophysiology: TSH stimulates hypertrophy and iodine uptake, increasing gland size.
Colloid accumulation also contributes to enlargement.
signs_symptoms: Feeling of pressure or difficulty swallowing.
Dry cough or hoarseness from laryngeal compression.
In hyperfunctioning goiter: weight loss, tremor, tachycardia.
diagnostics: TSH, T3, and T4 blood tests; high TSH suggests simple goiter.
Thyroid ultrasound: evaluates size and nodules presence.
Fine‑needle aspiration biopsy if nodule suspicious.
treatment: Levothyroxine if goiter associated with hypothyroidism.
Radioiodine or thyroidectomy for large or symptomatic goiter.
complications: Dysphagia and sensation of foreign body.
nursing_care: Assess size, consistency, and mobility of the goiter.
Monitor signs of respiratory compromise (respiratory rate, saturation).
Record TSH, T3, T4 values and compare with normal ranges.
Keep the patient’s head slightly elevated to aid breathing.
Prepare the patient for diagnostic tests (ultrasound, biopsy).
patient_teaching: Importance of a diet with adequate iodine (iodized salt, fish).
Take medication as prescribed and do not discontinue without indication.

outcomes: Activity level: will tolerate daily activities without excessive dyspnea in 1 week
Fatigue: will report decreased sense of tiredness in 5 days

interventions.action: Assess respiratory rate and effort level during routine activities.
interventions.rationale: Detect early signs of intolerance and guide activity modification.

interventions.action: Plan rest periods every 20‑30 minutes during prolonged activities.
interventions.rationale: Allows the patient to conserve energy and prevent exhaustion.

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing techniques.
interventions.rationale: Improves oxygenation and reduces sensation of breathlessness.

interventions.action: Coordinate with physician for adjustment of antithyroid drugs or levothyroxine based on lab results.
interventions.rationale: Controlling thyroid status reduces intolerance symptoms.

interventions.action: Record fatigue level using a 0‑10 scale before and after activity.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates assessment of progress and intervention effectiveness.

outcomes: Maintain neck skin integrity without irritation or ulcers

interventions.action: Observe signs of respiratory difficulty (cyanosis, accessory muscle use).
interventions.rationale: Identify need for intervention to prevent asphyxiation.

interventions.action: Keep the neck area free of tight clothing and objects that may press the gland.
interventions.rationale: Prevents increased compression and potential skin injury.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of avoiding sudden neck movements.
interventions.rationale: Reduces risk of trauma to an inflamed area.

interventions.action: Position the patient semi‑recumbent with back support.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates thoracic expansion and reduces airway pressure.

interventions.action: Document any changes in goiter size and notify the physician.
interventions.rationale: Allows timely intervention if the goiter progresses.

Medical-Surgical Nursing: Thyroid and Parathyroid Disorders

summary.0.quote: If a person’s diet lacks sufficient iodine, the thyroid gland may not be able to produce enough thyroid hormones, leading to an increase in thyroid-stimulating hormone production.

key_points.2.quote: While simple goiters are generally benign and not associated with cancer, they can cause discomfort or aesthetic concerns due to the visible swelling in the neck.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Dietary iodine is required for the synthesis of T3 and T4.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: When T3 and T4 cannot be produced, the loop becomes broken and TSH is secreted in increasing amounts.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: The accumulation of colloid increases the overall size of the thyroid gland, causing a condition called a goiter ( Figure 21.8 ).

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Risk factors for thyroid cancer include radiation exposure, low iodine diet, obesity, family history, and certain hereditary conditions.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: It occurs when the thyroid gland becomes larger than normal, leading to a noticeable lump or protrusion in the front of the neck.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Hyperthyroidism The overproduction of thyroid hormones, hyperthyroidism can lead to an increased metabolic rate and its effects: weight loss, excess heat production, sweating, and an increased heart rate.

sections.diagnostics.4.quote: A fine needle aspiration biopsy of the thyroid may also be done to rule out cancer.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Laboratory values, such as TSH, T3 , and T4 will be monitored to see if there is improvement in response to treatment.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: In many cases, the enlargement of the thyroid gland can be reversed with adequate intake of iodine through iodized salt or other dietary sources rich in iodine.
